title: Chicago permit expediting firm (BACP-licensed) with AI-assisted application prep
product_service: Preparing, filing and shepherding City of Chicago building, sign and demolition permit applications (plan-based and express), correction responses, status tracking, fee payment and inspection scheduling; AI used to pre-check completeness, draft correction responses and monitor status.
target_customer: Small/mid developers, commercial tenants doing build-outs, retail/restaurant chains' construction managers, sign companies, condo associations, out-of-town GCs and architects who do not self-file.
purchase_motivation: Time-to-permit drives carrying cost and delayed rent/opening; DOB process complexity; out-of-town firms lack local process knowledge; architects/GCs offload clerical filing.
spending_evidence: 6,428 of 32,032 Chicago permits issued in 2025 listed an expediter contact, incl. 2,567 of 5,505 renovation/alteration and 424 of 1,460 new-construction permits [A, WS10-S010]; the Public Building Commission ran a dedicated permit-expediter RFP with task orders [B, WS10-S009].
representative_operators: 204 distinct individual expediters appear on 2025 Chicago permits; top 10 handled 46.3% of expediter-listed permits, 34 handled >=50 each, the busiest 969 [A, WS10-S010]
revenue_mechanism: Per-permit flat fee by complexity plus hourly for corrections/meetings; City permit fees passed through; retainers for repeat filers.
typical_transaction_value: Private-market fee MISSING; one public-owner task order capped basic application services at $350 (2018) [B, WS10-S009]; hypothesis $500-$3,000 per plan-based permit [E].
direct_costs: W-2 expediter/coordinator labor, $300k+ CGL insurance naming the City, software, travel/parking.
contribution_profit_note: At hypothesized fees and ~5-15 staff hours per plan-based permit, ~$300-$2,000 contribution per permit [E].
working_capital_note: Invoiced per milestone, likely net-30 from architects/GCs; expediter may advance City permit fees and rebill (float risk) [E].
sales_cycle: Days-weeks for one permit; months to earn repeat relationships with architects/developers.
repeat_purchase: recurring-relationship: developers, chains and sign companies file many permits per year
acquisition_channels: Mine public permit records for high-volume owners/architects/GCs without an expediter [A, WS10-S010]
Construction managers of out-of-town retail/restaurant chains
customer_accessibility: Every permit lists contacts, so buyers are identifiable from open data; but incumbents hold long relationships and buyers need confidence in DOB process knowledge.
supplier_accessibility: Labor-based; experienced licensed expediters exist (204 active names) and could be hired as employees - assumed, unverified.
competitive_intensity: moderate: fragmented (204 names; top 10 = 46%) but relationship-driven [A, WS10-S010]
entry_strategy: Focus on underserved segments (out-of-town chains, 2-6 unit developers, ADU conversions, sign permits); sell speed SLAs and live status dashboards built on public permit data; hire one experienced expediter as employee from day one.
licenses: BACP expediter company license (MCC 4-6-250) plus individual expediter licence per filer (4-6-260); fingerprinting; >=$300,000 per-occurrence CGL naming the City; disqualified for fraud/bribery convictions; age 18+ [B, WS10-S009; A, WS10-S008]. Licence fee and processing time MISSING. Exempt from 'expediter' definition: licensed architects/engineers, the GC and licensed trade contractor on their own permits [B, WS10-S009]. Plan-based permits may only be filed by an Illinois-licensed architect/engineer or City-licensed expediter [A, WS10-S035].
regulatory_barriers: Strict false-statement/anti-bribery rules; ongoing Chicago Construction Codes Modernization (Phase 3 implementation Oct 2026 per DOB alerts) [A, WS10-S004] changes procedures; City self-service portals could reduce need.
operational_risks: Application errors cause rejections and reputation damage; review times outside the firm's control; key-person dependence on an experienced expediter.
financial_risks: Low: receivable delays and permit-fee float.
geographic_constraints: Licence and know-how are City-of-Chicago specific; each suburb has separate processes.
founder_expertise: Chicago Construction Codes administrative provisions, zoning basics, DOB e-Plan/Dynamic Portal workflows, correction handling; relationship selling to architects/GCs.
staffing: Founder + 1 experienced expediter (W-2) at launch; add coordinators as volume grows (assume ~300-500 permits per coordinator-year [E]).
automation_potential: AI: checklist completeness checks, document assembly, drafting correction responses, automated status monitoring from open data, client updates. Human: code/zoning judgment, City meetings, relationships. Real but moderate savings.
delegation_potential: Good: expediting is a standard employee role; SOP-friendly; founder can own sales.
scalability: Capped by Chicago permit volume (32,032 in 2025, down from 48,540 in 2019; 29,067 in 2026 through late Nov) [A, WS10-S010]; even the busiest expediter handled ~1,000 permits.
expansion: Suburban permit services; owner's-rep services (WS10-035); zoning/ADU feasibility packages; BACP business-licence expediting; permit-data products (WS10-006).
roic_note: Capital at risk <$15k; if $60-200k operating profit is reached, ROIC is several hundred percent [E].
critical_assumptions: Private-market fees of $500-$3,000 per plan-based permit [E]
A new firm can win 150-300 permits/yr by year 3 against relationship incumbents
An experienced licensed expediter can be hired at ~$55-75k [E]
unanswered_questions: BACP expediter company licence fee and processing time
Actual private fee schedules by permit type
Share of expediter-listed permits filed by in-house staff of architects/developers vs independent firms
Effect of 2026 code-modernization on filing complexity
failure_modes: Fee compression as architects self-file with better portals/AI
Permit volumes keep falling in the 7%+ mortgage-rate environment

staffing: DCP (PE or NICET III layout) and at least one licensed inspector at day one.
automation_potential: Inspection scheduling, digital reports, deficiency-to-quote automation, compliance-portal uploads; hands-on testing remains human.
delegation_potential: High once licensed staff are in place; licensed roles are standard in industry.
scalability: Strong - installed-base service with repair pull-through; prime target for consolidators.
expansion: Fire pumps, standpipes, backflow on fire lines, alarm ITM, special hazards.
